title: Containerized pipeline skeleton + CI smoke test (Nextflow/nf-core-style)
context: All downstream reanalysis tasks depend on a containerized pipeline skeleton that enforces the reproducibility standard from M0. The skeleton must integrate the workflow manager (Nextflow/nf-core-style), reference containers by immutable digest, and include a CI smoke test to prove end-to-end execution before any real dataset work begins. This is the foundational infrastructure all subsequent pipeline tasks build on.
objective: Implement the containerized pipeline skeleton with a Nextflow (nf-core-style) workflow that references containers by immutable digest, passes a CI smoke test end-to-end, and lays the plumbing for the provenance/run-manifest generation required by the reproducibility standard.
acceptanceCriteria: A Nextflow (DSL2, nf-core-style) pipeline skeleton is committed that references all containers by immutable digest (sha256:...) — no floating tags.
A CI smoke test runs the skeleton end-to-end on a trivial synthetic input and passes, confirming the workflow manager and container plumbing work.

The skeleton includes stub stages for spectrum processing, search/identification, FDR, quantification, and run-manifest emission — stubbed, not implemented — to define the interface for subsequent tasks.
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass for any TypeScript tooling committed alongside the pipeline.
Pipeline code is MIT-licensed; commit is DCO signed-off.
resources: PLAN.md — Solution approach & architecture, Tech stack section
proteomics-reanalysis-repro-standard-003 (reproducibility standard must be ratified first)
output: A committed containerized Nextflow pipeline skeleton with a passing CI smoke test and stub stages for each analysis phase, ready for the DDA reanalysis task to fill in.
